In the cells of human body, enzymes continuously convert toxic chemicals into harmless products to prevent the accumulation of toxic chemicals.

This process occurs efficiently inside the cells because enzymes
explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that lower activation energy, accelerating biochemical reactions by up to millions of times (high catalytic turnover rate). This enables cells to neutralize potentially lethal toxins (e.g. catalase converting $H_2O_2$ into $H_2O$ and $O_2$) before toxic metabolites can accumulate.

explanation: The optimum pH of an enzyme is the pH at which its reaction rate is fastest, meaning it requires the shortest time to completely hydrolyze the substrate. In test tube IV (pH 7), complete breakdown occurs in only 60 seconds, which is faster than in test tubes I, II, or III.

explanation: Dietary fibre (roughage) is indigestible plant cellulose that retains water and adds bulk to fecal matter, stimulating gastrointestinal peristalsis. explanation: The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice containing digestive enzymes including pancreatic amylase (for carbohydrates) and pancreatic lipase (for lipids).
